paper.title: CoCoDA: Co-evolving Compositional DAG for Tool-Augmented Agents
paper.central_claim: A single compositional code DAG (typed signature, description, pre/post spec, examples per tool) lets a small planner and its tool library co-evolve: Typed DAG Retrieval keeps prompt cost sublinear in library size, validated composite tools are folded from successful trajectories by a fixed teacher, and a DAG-induced saved-call reward trains the planner with GRPO; an 8B student matches or exceeds a 32B teacher on GSM8K and MATH and beats tool-use and library-learning baselines.

evidence.quote: scaling the tool library creates a coupled challenge: the library must evolve with the planner as new reusable subroutines emerge, while retrieval from the growing library must remain within a fixed context budget.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: co-evolution of library and planner plus bounded retrieval.

evidence.quote: a hierarchy is either code-aware or built for an LLM under a fixed context budget , never both.
evidence.support_explanation: Positioning claim of a missing quadrant against DreamCoder/Stitch, CodeRAG, RAPTOR, Voyager/CRAFT/CREATOR/TroVE; only ReTool, ToRL, ReAct, CREATOR, TroVE are run.

evidence.quote: Successful trajectories are passed to a fixed teacher abstractor, which proposes composite tools. A proposal is committed only if it preserves acyclicity and satisfies dependency and specification checks.
evidence.support_explanation: Library edits are written by a fixed stronger teacher (Qwen3-32B), not by the student; commit gate = successful trajectory (R_res >= rho) + acyclicity + LLM-checked specs + dedup merge.

evidence.quote: The planner is updated with a DAG-induced reward that credits tools by their primitive expansion size
evidence.support_explanation: GAR: reward bonus lambda * sum (flat(t) - 1) per invoked tool, lambda=0.20.

evidence.quote: Typed DAG Retrieval prunes candidates by symbolic signature unification, ranks survivors by descriptions, filters them by behavioral specifications, and disambiguates with examples, keeping expensive context materialization on progressively smaller candidate sets.
evidence.support_explanation: Four-stage cascade L1-L4; only L1 is symbolic.

evidence.quote: and treats them as a hard accept/reject judged by the planner under the prompt of Appendix D.5
evidence.support_explanation: Specification filtering and semantic ranking are done by the (small) planner itself; the claim that a surviving composite is certified equivalent (Theorem 3) rests on faithful LLM reading.

evidence.quote: CoCoDA wins every (size, benchmark) cell and beats the strongest tool-augmented baseline, ReTool, by up to
evidence.support_explanation: Per Table 1 at 8B: margins over ReTool are +0.85 GSM8K, +1.34 MATH, +1.18 WTQ, +0.51 FinQA, +0.91 EvalPlus, +1.01 MBPP; test-set sizes range from 164 to 5,000.

evidence.quote: recovering teacher-level performance at roughly a quarter of the parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher row is no-tool CoT (93.40/61.62); student CoT is already 89.84/60.80 and ReTool 92.82/61.84, so MATH parity with the teacher also holds for ReTool.

evidence.quote: All baselines share the student backbone and task prompts.
evidence.support_explanation: Training data, teacher access, cold-start SFT, steps and compute for baselines are not described.

evidence.quote: also trains a tool-integrated reasoner with GRPO-style updates and shares our RL backbone, but keeps the tool inventory frozen throughout training, isolating the contribution of library co-evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: ReTool is the intended control for library co-evolution.

evidence.quote: Each variant retrains the 4B student under identical hyperparameters, replacing only the ablated component with its non-structural counterpart (flat library, dense retrieval, plain reward)
evidence.support_explanation: Component ablations (CTD/TDR/GAR) at 4B; single table without per-cell SD.

evidence.quote: equivalent to a GRPO-trained ReTool-style planner over a flat pool of tools collected from the warm-start phase.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors state the all-off ablation equals a ReTool-style planner, yet Table 2 gives 87.96/54.27/41.38 on GSM8K/MATH/WTQ versus ReTool 4B 91.05/58.41/46.72 in Table 1.

evidence.quote: Disabling all three barely beats plain CoT, confirming the components are complementary.
evidence.support_explanation: All-off 4B average is within ~0.2-0.5 pts of 4B CoT on several tasks (GSM8K 87.96 vs 87.79).

evidence.quote: so that the ablation isolates the mechanism rather than the coefficient schedule.
evidence.support_explanation: lambda is not re-tuned per ablation; a re-tuned version is said to be within 0.3 points (not shown).

evidence.quote: standard deviation is at most 0.4 0.4 on GSM8K/MATH/WTQ/FinQA and at most 0.7 0.7 on EvalPlus/MBPP.
evidence.support_explanation: Three seeds {13, 42, 2026}; only upper bounds of SD given in prose, no per-cell SD in tables, none for ablation; HumanEval+ has 164 problems.

evidence.quote: We use the official train/test splits for GSM8K, MATH, WTQ, FinQA, and MBPP, and the full EvalPlus suite (extended HumanEval with hardened unit tests) for code generation.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 6 lists EvalPlus with no training split; how the EvalPlus student/library is trained is not stated.

evidence.quote: Both rise sharply in the first
evidence.support_explanation: Library size and depth saturate after about 150 steps; End-of-training libraries hold 183-364 composites, max depth 3-4, 61-158 rejected proposals (Table 5).

evidence.quote: while latency grows roughly linearly
evidence.support_explanation: Accuracy plateaus by about 400 tools; the evolved libraries are at most ~380 tools, so the context-budget bottleneck in the motivation is not binding in the trained regime; Fig 2(b) sweeps to 1,600 nodes on a fixed snapshot.

evidence.quote: Flat retrieval embeds and ranks all four annotation levels per node (no hierarchy; typical prior baseline).
evidence.support_explanation: Retrieval-cost comparison at matched 4B accuracy: flat about 11.4x and RAPTOR-style text hierarchy about 4.7x TDR's tokens at 1,600 nodes (Fig 2b).

evidence.quote: 1,873 1{,}873 library tools → \to 41 41 type-compatible candidates per sub-goal.
evidence.support_explanation: Case study cites 1,873 library tools for a GSM8K query, while Table 5 gives 309 tools (18 primitives + 291 composites) for GSM8K and Table 4 lists a 42-primitive shared set versus 14-22 primitives per benchmark in Table 5; internal numbers do not reconcile.

evidence.quote: Intuitively, new library entries cannot crowd out previously retrieved tools unless they are strictly better substitutes.
evidence.support_explanation: Theorem 4 (monotone co-evolution) rests on this retrieval-consistency assumption and on a trust-region GRPO lemma; it concerns the shaped objective J = R_res + lambda R_comp, and the assumption is not tested empirically.

evidence.quote: The deduplication prompt (Appendix D.8 ) returns MERGE
evidence.support_explanation: Near-duplicate merging is decided by an LLM prompt; spec validation of composites is also LLM-based; only acyclicity is checked programmatically.

evidence.quote: Qwen3-32B serves as the teacher for tool extraction and solution generation; smaller students are trained via GRPO.
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher also generates cold-start SFT demonstrations (Stage 2); the student thus receives teacher supervision twice (SFT and tool library).

evidence.quote: Table 7 reports end-to-end wall-clock training time and GPU-hours per student size.
evidence.support_explanation: 35-98 GPU-hours for CoCoDA on 4 H200; baseline training cost not reported.

evidence.quote: We provide theoretical results showing retrieval cost reduction, sublinear retrieval time, compositional advantage under the shaped reward, monotone co-evolution under conservative updates, and DAG well-formedness.
evidence.support_explanation: Five conditional results (assumptions on level costs, retrieval consistency, trust-region GRPO); theory not accompanied by checks of its assumptions.

Our reading: full CoCoDA beats the fixed-inventory ReTool control by 0.1-1.6 pts at 4B; removing the structure drops 3.5-5.2 pts below the full model and 3-5 pts below ReTool, so the structural parts mainly repair the harm of a growing flat library rather than add a large gain over a fixed tool set.

evidence.quote: Experiments on GSM8K and MATH show that an 8B student matches or exceeds its 32B teacher, with the largest gains at the smallest student sizes.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim; gains over vanilla CoT are largest for 0.6B and shrink with scale (8B CoT already close).

signatures.object: Compositional tool DAG (primitive and composite executable tools with typed signature, description, pre/post spec, examples) that a small planner reads through a four-stage retrieval cascade; baseline = flat/fixed tool inventory (ReTool, ToRL) and flat library learners (CREATOR, TroVE)
signatures.information: Successful training trajectories (R_res >= 0.8), current library signatures, teacher Qwen3-32B abstraction prompt; planner sees only retrieved tool cards; test tasks not used for library building
signatures.operation: Per query: retrieve typed candidates (L1 symbolic, L2 top-32 by planner, L3 spec check, L4 example rerank), sample G=8 rollouts, GRPO on R_res + 0.2*sum(flat(t)-1); for successful rollouts the teacher proposes composites that InsertTool validates (children specs, acyclicity), dedups (MERGE) or adds
signatures.output: Updated library (V, E, I) and updated planner weights per query step
signatures.conditions: verifiable tasks (exec/exact-match/unit tests), typed Python-like tools, three online epochs, 64 queries per step
signatures.feedback: deterministic verifier result and saved-call credit
signatures.selection_rule_data: library writes require successful rollout and passing validation; planner chosen after fixed epochs; no held-out gate for composites; no retirement of tools
signatures.persistence: tool library grows monotonically (rejected proposals dropped); planner weights saved
signatures.later_use: retrieved on later queries and at test time via TDR
signatures.claimed_effect: 8B: GSM8K 93.67, MATH 63.18 vs ReTool 92.82/61.84 and teacher CoT 93.40/61.62; wins all 24 (size, benchmark) cells
signatures.failure_boundary: teacher-written library; LLM-judged spec checks; dependence on typed code tools; library plateau ~400 tools; no tool retirement

signatures.object: Planner (student LLM) weights trained with graph-aware GRPO and teacher cold-start SFT
signatures.operation: SFT on teacher demonstrations over a warm library then online GRPO with saved-call reward
signatures.persistence: weights (outside harness scope; the library is the retained non-weight component)
signatures.failure_boundary: reward can favor deep composites when primitives would suffice (lambda too large lowers accuracy)

gap.author_gap: Prior tool/skill libraries are flat or text-indexed, so prompt cost grows with library size and code structure is hidden; code-aware hierarchies are not built for token-budgeted LLM planners.
gap.checked_gap: Plausible but partly rhetorical: the 'missing quadrant' framing is asserted; the cost bottleneck is not binding in the trained regime (libraries 183-364 composites, accuracy plateau at ~400 tools); Voyager/CRAFT/ReGAL/TroVE-style libraries are cited but only CREATOR and TroVE are run; code-hierarchy retrieval neighbors (RAPTOR-style, CodeRAG-style) appear only in the retrieval-cost sweep.

CREATOR, TroVE, LATM, CRAFT, ReGAL, Voyager (offline or flat-text skill/tool libraries)

lineage_closest_adjacent.solved: code-aware or LLM-aware hierarchy, not both

gap.residue: Joint growth of an executable library and a planner that uses it under bounded context.
gap.stakes: Prompt cost and retrieval errors as a library scales to thousands of tools.
gap.method_response: Typed DAG with cost-ordered cascade retrieval, validated composite insertion from teacher abstraction, and a saved-call reward.
gap.remaining_gap: Teacher dependence, spec validation by LLM judgment, no tool retirement, benefit over fixed-inventory RL control is about one point, scaling claim not exercised by trained libraries.
unresolved: Whether a static teacher-built library plus the same RL would match CoCoDA (co-evolution not isolated)

tactic_steps_checked: planner decomposes the query into typed sub-goals and routes each to retrieved executable tools via a structured typed artifact; execution results (verifier) close the loop and drive credit
accumulates verified composites into a reusable library (success condition on reusable capital)
matches.success_checks: typed, machine-checkable handoff present (signature unification, contracts, examples); load-bearing mechanism ablated (CTD, TDR, GAR) but the all-off variant falls below the fixed-inventory ReTool control, so the ablation does not collapse to a named baseline; prompts disclosed; cost reported partly
matches.failure_checks: multi-stage pipeline of existing parts risk; spec checks judged by an LLM rather than a sound solver for the retrieval gate
matches.reason: Tool execution is the sound solver and typed sub-goals are the interface (C25 tactic); the novelty sits in the library structure and credit. The learned planner is also the ranker/spec judge, which departs from delegating verifiable work to a sound external component.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS C25: structured artifacts routed to a sound solver with verified by-products accumulated into reusable capital. Domain H08: executable skills organized as a typed DAG, composed and promoted with validation.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: H08 expects trace-level responsibility, localized repair and rollback protecting mature skills; CoCoDA has none (append-only). C25 expects a sound solver at the retrieval gate; CoCoDA uses the planner for ranking and spec checking.

claims.text: CoCoDA beats strong tool-augmented and library-learning baselines in every size/benchmark cell
claims.baseline_control: CoT, ReAct, ToRL, ReTool, CREATOR, TroVE
claims.selection_vs_test: official test splits; library built on training stream
claims.result_denominator: margins over ReTool 0.1-2.0 pts (8B: +0.5 to +1.3); test sizes 164-5,000; SD <= 0.4/0.7
claims.counterevidence: Margins close to 1-3 SD on large sets and inside noise on HumanEval+ (164 problems); teacher access of baselines unspecified.
claims.allowed_conclusion: CoCoDA is consistently slightly ahead of the best RL baseline in author-reported means.

claims.text: An 8B student matches or exceeds the 32B teacher on GSM8K and MATH
claims.setting: 8B student with tools vs 32B teacher CoT
claims.counterevidence: Comparator is a no-tool teacher; 8B CoT is already 89.84/60.80 and ReTool 92.82/61.84.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Tool-integrated RL students approach a no-tool 32B teacher; not specific to the library.

claims.text: Each of CTD, TDR and GAR contributes
claims.baseline_control: flat library, flat dense retrieval, exec-only reward
claims.counterevidence: All-off variant (87.96 GSM8K) is 3 pts below ReTool (91.05) although described as ReTool-like; no per-cell SD; no static-library control.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Structure helps relative to an unstructured growing library; incremental benefit over a fixed inventory is about one point.

claims.text: Typed DAG Retrieval keeps context cost sublinear and far below flat/text-hierarchy retrieval
claims.setting: fixed CoCoDA snapshot swept from 50 to 1,600 nodes at matched 4B accuracy
claims.counterevidence: Sweep exceeds sizes actually evolved (<= ~380 tools); Assumption 1 constants not measured.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Cascade retrieval is much cheaper than flat retrieval at large synthetic library sizes.

claims.text: Co-evolution is monotone and DAG well-formed (theory)
claims.counterevidence: Assumptions untested; monotone claim concerns the shaped objective, not accuracy.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Acyclicity by construction; monotonicity is conditional.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: A teacher-built, typed executable tool DAG co-trained with a GRPO planner gives small, consistent test-accuracy gains (about 0.5-2 points) over a fixed-inventory RL tool-use baseline at four student sizes, and the cascade retrieval is much cheaper than flat retrieval at large library sizes (author-reported, 3 seeds).
assessment.not_supported: That library co-evolution itself (vs static teacher library + RL, teacher SFT, or better RL) drives the gains; self-discovery of tools (teacher writes them); scalability in the trained regime; certified composite equivalence; fair parity of baselines; teacher-parity beyond the no-tool CoT comparison.
assessment.note: Author-reported results only; not reproduced. Partially weight-training: library is the retained non-weight component, planner weights are trained.

G.reason: Coupled library-growth/retrieval-cost framing is real and the lineage is broad, but the bottleneck does not bind in the trained regime, the 'missing quadrant' claim is asserted, and most named neighbors (Voyager, CRAFT, ReGAL, DreamCoder, RAPTOR-style) are not run against.

M.reason: Typed cascade, validated composite insertion and saved-call reward form a coherent, reconstructable design aimed at the stated cost and credit problems; the planner doubles as ranker/spec judge, spec equivalence is LLM-judged, and reward may over-favor composites.

X.reason: Algorithms, prompts, hyperparameters, rejection examples and library statistics are fully given; commit gate is verified success + acyclicity + LLM spec check + dedup, but no tool retirement, versioning or rollback, teacher-written tools, and internal numbers (tool counts, primitive sets) do not reconcile.

E.measurement.reason: Deterministic verifiers on six benchmarks with large test sets except HumanEval+ (164); comparators are mixed (no-tool teacher), retrieval-token cost measured; scalability sweep uses sizes not reached by trained libraries.

E.causality.reason: Component ablations and a fixed-inventory RL control exist, but co-evolution is not isolated from teacher SFT/library or a static-library control, all-off variant lies far below the ReTool control it is said to equal, baseline teacher parity unknown, no per-cell SD.

E.holdout.reason: Official test splits with library and planner built on training streams across six benchmarks and four sizes; EvalPlus training source is unspecified and no explicit leakage guard or per-tool held-out admission test is stated.

E.statistics.reason: Three seeds with SD upper bounds stated in prose but not shown per cell, ablation without SD, no tests; many margins about 1 point on benchmarks with 164-1,319 problems.

E.cost.reason: GPU-hours and wall-clock per student size and token cost of retrieval versus flat/text-hierarchy substrates at matched accuracy are reported; teacher-call cost and baseline training cost are missing.

status.reason: Complete HTML full text including appendices, prompts and proofs read; figure images not available as text.
